question: I am currently working on a production line equipped with an IPC, several PLCs, and several drives all interconnected and communicating over a CAN network. Yesterday, we encountered multiple communication alarms associated with most devices on the network. To diagnose the issue, I initially checked the CAN high and low voltages, which were within acceptable ranges: CAN H ranged between 2.6 to 2.9V and CAN L between 2.1 to 2.5V. Subsequently, I powered off the system and measured the resistance between CAN H and CAN L, which read 43 ohms. Considering there should be two 120-ohm terminating resistors at each end, I expected the measurement to be around 60 ohms. One aspect that confused me is the presence of multiple CAN adapters. Some of these adapters split the CAN signal into two separate loops, each with its own set of resistors. I'm unsure whether these additional loops and resistors constitute separate networks or if they are part of the network I am troubleshooting. The specific network I am focusing on is highlighted with green boxes in the attached picture and the other loops connected to the same adapter are in red. Don't know if they affect my network or not since they are coming out of the same adapter. After noticing the 43-ohm reading, I suspected unnecessary resistors might be affecting the network. As a test, I turned off the terminator switch at the last node, increasing the network's resistance to 70 ohms.
evidence_quote: if R < 50 Ω the reason may be a redundant termination resistor or a short
